title: Conway keeps New Zealand afloat after Pant's ton powers India to record 720
excerpt: The visitors declared on 720/9, their third-highest Test total, before claiming two wickets in the final session.
author: Cricbuzz Staff
body: Rishabh Pant's century and Dhruv Jurel's 78 extended India's prolific batting show in Wellington before the visitors declared at 720 for 9 - their third-highest total in Test cricket - to take a lead of 352 on Day 4 of the first Test. India also made early inroads in New Zealand's second innings, but a patient half-century from Devon Conway helped the hosts stem the damage as they ended the day at 119 for 2, still trailing by 233.

At the start of the day, nightwatchman Anshul Kamboj came out firing on all cylinders, striking two fours each off Kyle Jamieson and Nathan Smith in the first three overs to take India past 500. Pant joined the charge with a four and a six off Jamieson as the fifth-wicket pair brought up a half-century stand. It was the first time India had recorded fifty-plus partnerships for each of their first five wickets in an overseas Test. Kamboj also launched Glenn Phillips over deep midwicket for six as India made brisk progress on the fourth morning. He contributed 38 to a 68-run stand with Pant before falling to Phillips inside the first hour of play.

The New Zealand bowlers continued to toil on a flat wicket as Jurel got going with a couple of fours, while Pant raced towards the three-figure mark with strokes all around the park. A boundary off Jacob Duffy took him into the 90s before he struck a four and a six off Phillips to bring up a 135-ball century, becoming the sixth Indian to score hundreds in all SENA countries. Jurel added another boundary off Duffy before Pant struck two more sixes off Phillips as India powered past 600 for the first time against New Zealand, and extended their lead beyond 250.

Pant's fine innings, however, came to an end in the final over before Lunch when he holed out to deep midwicket off Rachin Ravindra. His dismissal ended a 75-run partnership with Jurel, making it only the fifth instance in Test cricket of a team recording fifty-plus partnerships for each of its first six wickets in an innings. India went into the break having added 143 runs in 27.5 overs at a scoring rate of 5.14, taking their lead to 261.

A steady partnership between Jurel and Washington Sundar prolonged New Zealand's misery. It was Jurel's turn to get the next fifty-plus score in the innings, which he got with a boundary off Daryl Mitchell, and another four off the same bowler took India's lead past 300. Another half-century partnership was raised - the first time in the history of Test cricket that a team had 50-plus stands in an innings for each of the first seven wickets - before Washington was bowled by Ravindra for 24. Akash Deep then hit two sixes in an over of Phillips before the offspinner bagged his wicket.

The onslaught continued and India crossed 700, with Jurel striking a four and a six off Phillips to take the lead past 350. Phillips, however, ended Jurel's stay by having him stumped, bagging his third wicket to leave India nine down. India declared soon after the dismissal, having posted the highest total in Tests against New Zealand, and also the highest in New Zealand. Meanwhile, Duffy finished with figures of 1 for 201, becoming only the third bowler to concede 200 or more in an innings.

With a mountain to climb in the third innings, New Zealand found themselves in early trouble as Tom Latham bagged a pair, edging Jasprit Bumrah behind in the opening over. Henry Nicholls got a few boundaries and was saved by the umpire's call of not-out for lbw when he decided to shoulder arms to a Bumrah delivery and India went for the DRS. Conway, who struck a couple of fours, remained unbeaten along with Nicholls as they negotiated the 11-over passage before Tea without further damage.

There was still no assistance from the pitch for the bowlers as New Zealand's second wicket pair made steady progress, bringing up a half-century stand early in the final session. India tried unorthodox fields, using close-in fielders on the legside, bowling tight lines and keeping things quiet, trying to unsettle New Zealand in a battle of patience. It worked, as the in-form Nicholls got an inside edge onto his thigh pad off Prasidh Krishna, with Jurel taking a splendid catch diving forward from a slightly deep short-leg position, to leave New Zealand at 60 for 2.

Ravindra was stuck on zero for 14 deliveries before getting off the mark with a boundary to fine leg. He settled into a good partnership with Conway as the left-handed pair kept the Indian bowlers at bay. Conway brought up his fifty with a pull for a four off Prasidh, taking New Zealand past 100. Prasidh bowled an impressive spell, keeping the two batters on their toes, but wasn't able to break through as Conway and Ravindra saw through the remainder of the day's play, having added 59 runs.

Brief scores: New Zealand 368 & 119/2 (Devon Conway 59*, Henry Nicholls 31; Prasidh Krishna 1-20) trail India 720/9 decl. (KL Rahul 136, Rishabh Pant 128, Shubman Gill 98, Yashasvi Jaiswal 85, Devdutt Padikkal 80, Dhruv Jurel 78; Glenn Phillips 3-154) by 233 runs.
